lessons.title: Ma voix spéciale
lessons.oneGoal: Students discover their voice as a tool for communication

opening.activity: Explore different voices - whisper, loud, high, low. Point to throat and say 'voix'. Everyone practices saying their name with their special voice.

mainActivity.activity: Voice exploration games - students experiment with volume, pitch, and expression. Practice 'Bonjour' in different ways. Record some voices if technology available.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may be naturally expressive, others shy. Support all comfort levels with voice exploration.

closing.activity: Circle sharing - each student says one word in their special voice. Celebrate the uniqueness of each voice.

decisionPoints: If students too shy to use voices → Start with whispering or humming, gradually increase comfort
If students get too loud → Channel energy into controlled voice exploration with volume levels
If students have speech differences → Celebrate all voices as special and valuable communication tools
lessons.troubleshooting: If voice exploration feels uncomfortable, use familiar songs or chants as starting point
lessons.realWorldConnection: We use our voices every day to talk to family and friends - our voice is special and unique
lessons.progression: Foundation lesson - introduces voice as communication tool

lessons.title: Montrer et dire
lessons.oneGoal: Students bring something special to share with simple French words

opening.activity: Review using our voices. Today we use voice to share special things. Model with teacher's special item.

mainActivity.activity: Traditional show and tell with French vocabulary support. Students show item and say 2-3 simple French words about it. Use 'Voici...' and 'J'aime...' sentence starters.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may have elaborate presentations, others just show and say one word. Both are perfect.

closing.activity: Reflection on sharing - students say one thing they learned about a classmate today.

decisionPoints: If students forgot to bring items → Use classroom objects or let them share about favorite thing at home
If students use only English → Provide French word cards and gentle modeling
If presentations take too long → Use timer and celebrate concise sharing
lessons.troubleshooting: If students are nervous about presenting, let them share with just teacher or one friend first
lessons.realWorldConnection: Show and tell helps us share what's important to us - just like telling family about special things
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by using voice to share personal items

lessons.title: Gestes qui parlent
lessons.oneGoal: Students use gestures and body language to communicate meaning

opening.activity: Review using voice to share. Today explore how body 'talks' too. Model gestures for hello, goodbye, happy, sad.

mainActivity.activity: Gesture games - students communicate ideas using only body language, then add French words. Practice common gestures and their meanings.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural movers, others more reserved. Support all styles of physical expression.

closing.activity: Silent communication challenge - students communicate one idea to partner using only gestures.

decisionPoints: If students uncomfortable with movement → Start with simple hand gestures before full body movement
If students get too silly → Channel energy into purposeful gesture communication
If students have mobility differences → Adapt gestures to individual abilities
lessons.troubleshooting: If gesture communication feels abstract, use familiar actions like waving, clapping, pointing
lessons.realWorldConnection: Our bodies help us communicate even without words - like waving hello or pointing to things we want
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by adding non-verbal communication

lessons.title: Écouter avec attention
lessons.oneGoal: Students practice being good listeners and asking simple questions

opening.activity: Review using voice and body to communicate. Today focus on the other side - listening! Put on 'listening ears'.

mainActivity.activity: Listening practice with partners - one student shares, other practices active listening and asking simple questions using 'Qu'est-ce que...?' and 'Pourquoi...?'
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students naturally good listeners, others need reminders. Support development of listening skills.

closing.activity: Reflect on what makes good listening. Students share what they learned by listening carefully today.

decisionPoints: If students struggle with listening → Use visual cues and shorter sharing segments
If students ask too many questions → Help them focus on just one good question
If students interrupt often → Practice taking turns with visual or physical cues
lessons.troubleshooting: If listening skills are challenging, use structured turn-taking with clear signals for speaker/listener roles
lessons.realWorldConnection: Good communication means both talking and listening - like how family members take turns sharing
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by focusing on the listening side of communication

lessons.title: Raconter mes aventures
lessons.oneGoal: Students tell simple personal stories using sequence words

opening.activity: Review good listening and sharing. Today tell adventure stories! Model simple adventure with sequence words.

mainActivity.activity: Students share simple personal adventures (playground, home, weekend) using 'D'abord...', 'Ensuite...', 'Finalement...' Support with visual sequence cards.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may have elaborate adventures, others simple daily experiences. All stories are valuable.

closing.activity: Celebrate adventurous storytellers. Practice sequence words together as group.

decisionPoints: If students can't think of adventures → Help them identify simple daily experiences as adventures
If students get confused with sequence → Use visual timeline supports and practice with simple examples
If stories become very long → Help them focus on just 3 main parts
lessons.troubleshooting: If sequence concepts are difficult, use familiar classroom routine as practice for 'first, then, last'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We tell family about our adventures and experiences - sharing stories helps us remember and connect
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by structuring personal storytelling

lessons.title: Personnages vivants
lessons.oneGoal: Students use different voices and movements for simple characters

opening.activity: Review adventure storytelling. Today make characters come alive with special voices and movements!

mainActivity.activity: Character exploration - students practice different character voices (big/small, happy/sad, fast/slow) and movements. Create simple character scenarios.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural performers, others more reserved. Support all levels of character exploration.

closing.activity: Character parade - students briefly demonstrate their favorite character voice and movement.

decisionPoints: If students too shy for character work → Start with just voice changes, add movement gradually
If students get overly silly → Channel creativity into purposeful character development
If students copy each other → Encourage unique interpretations while validating similarities
lessons.troubleshooting: If character work feels too complex, start with familiar animals or family member voices
lessons.realWorldConnection: We change our voices when we pretend to be different people - like when playing with toys or telling stories
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by adding character work to storytelling

lessons.title: Émotions expressives
lessons.oneGoal: Students express different emotions through voice and face

opening.activity: Review character voices. Today explore how emotions change our voice and face. Model happy vs. sad voice.

mainActivity.activity: Emotion exploration - students practice expressing different emotions through facial expressions and voice tone. Use scenarios to practice appropriate emotional responses.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students very expressive, others more subtle. Support all styles of emotional expression.

closing.activity: Emotion check-in - students share how they're feeling using French emotion words and expressions.

decisionPoints: If students uncomfortable with emotional expression → Start with basic happy/sad, gradually add complexity
If students get too dramatic → Help them find appropriate levels of emotional expression
If students struggle identifying emotions → Use clear visual supports and modeling
lessons.troubleshooting: If emotion work feels too personal, use characters or stuffed animals to explore emotional expression
lessons.realWorldConnection: Our faces and voices show how we feel - helping others understand our emotions
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by adding emotional expression

lessons.title: Jouer des scènes
lessons.oneGoal: Students act out simple everyday scenarios with partners

opening.activity: Review expressing emotions. Today combine everything to act out real-life scenes with partners!

mainActivity.activity: Partner drama - students act out simple scenarios (ordering food, asking for help, greeting friends) using voice, emotion, and character skills.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some pairs may work smoothly, others need more structure. Support collaboration skills.

closing.activity: Mini performances - few pairs share their scenes with class. Celebrate teamwork and creativity.

decisionPoints: If partners have conflicts → Provide structured roles and clear expectations for cooperation
If students too shy for performance → Let them practice with teacher or perform for just one other pair
If scenes become too complex → Help simplify to just 2-3 exchanges
lessons.troubleshooting: If partner work is challenging, let students work individually or provide very structured role assignments
lessons.realWorldConnection: We act out different situations in our daily play - practicing helps us in real situations
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by combining skills in dramatic play

lessons.title: Présenter mes créations
lessons.oneGoal: Students present their artwork or projects with simple descriptions

opening.activity: Review acting scenes together. Today be solo presenters sharing our own special creations!

mainActivity.activity: Art presentation - students present their artwork or projects using simple French descriptions. Practice explaining process and meaning.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may give detailed presentations, others just show and say few words. Support all levels.

closing.activity: Audience appreciation - students practice giving positive feedback using simple French phrases.

decisionPoints: If students don't have artwork ready → Use any classroom work or let them draw simple picture quickly
If presentations too long → Use timer and help students focus on main points
If students very nervous → Let them present to small group first or have friend support them
lessons.troubleshooting: If presentation anxiety is high, let students practice explanation with just teacher before group presentation
lessons.realWorldConnection: Artists explain their work to help others understand - sharing our creations spreads joy
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by presenting personal work

lessons.title: Questions curieuses
lessons.oneGoal: Students ask thoughtful questions about classmates' presentations

opening.activity: Review presenting our work. Today be curious audience members who ask great questions!

mainActivity.activity: Question practice - students present briefly while others practice asking thoughtful questions using 'Pourquoi...?', 'Comment...?', 'Qu'est-ce que...?'
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural questioners, others need prompting. Support development of curiosity skills.

closing.activity: Celebrate good questions asked today. Discuss how questions help us learn about each other.

decisionPoints: If students ask inappropriate questions → Model respectful, relevant questioning
If students too shy to ask questions → Provide question sentence starters and encouragement
If same students always ask questions → Encourage quieter students with gentle prompting
lessons.troubleshooting: If questioning feels awkward, use familiar topics and model enthusiastic curiosity about simple things
lessons.realWorldConnection: Asking questions shows we're interested in others - curiosity helps us learn and make friends
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by becoming active audience members

lessons.title: Instructions claires
lessons.oneGoal: Students give simple instructions for games or activities

opening.activity: Review asking good questions. Today give clear instructions to help others learn new things!

mainActivity.activity: Instruction practice - students teach classmates simple games, activities, or skills using clear French instructions. Practice giving and following instructions.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural teachers, others need support organizing thoughts. Help all students practice instruction-giving.

closing.activity: Reflect on what makes instructions easy to follow. Celebrate successful teaching moments.

decisionPoints: If instructions too complex → Help students break down into simple steps
If students frustrated when others don't understand → Model patience and repeat instructions differently
If students can't think of what to teach → Provide simple activity options or classroom routines
lessons.troubleshooting: If instruction-giving is overwhelming, start with very familiar activities like hand-washing or line-up procedures
lessons.realWorldConnection: We give instructions to help others learn new things - like teaching friends games or showing family how to do something
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by using communication to guide others

lessons.title: Descriptions vivantes
lessons.oneGoal: Students describe people, places, or things with vivid details

opening.activity: Review giving clear instructions. Today paint pictures with words using vivid descriptions!

mainActivity.activity: Description practice - students describe pictures, objects, or experiences using sensory details and descriptive French words. Help others 'see' through words.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students naturally descriptive, others need prompting for details. Support development of descriptive language.

closing.activity: Guessing game - students give descriptions while others guess what they're describing.

decisionPoints: If students use only basic words → Provide descriptive word banks and model rich language
If descriptions too long → Help students focus on most important or interesting details
If students struggle with details → Use guided questions about colors, size, feelings, etc.
lessons.troubleshooting: If descriptive language feels difficult, start with familiar objects and use sensory exploration
lessons.realWorldConnection: Good descriptions help others picture what we're talking about - like describing a movie to someone who hasn't seen it
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by adding descriptive language skills

lessons.title: Spectacle de classe
lessons.oneGoal: Students perform in a simple class presentation showcasing their skills

opening.activity: Review all communication skills learned. Today put everything together in special class performance!

mainActivity.activity: Class show - students choose how to showcase their communication skills (storytelling, character work, presentations, etc.) in mini-performances.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may want elaborate performances, others simple sharing. Support all performance comfort levels.

closing.activity: Audience appreciation and celebration of everyone's communication growth. Take photos of proud performers.

decisionPoints: If students nervous about performing → Offer options like partnering or performing for smaller groups
If students want very long performances → Help them choose one or two skills to showcase
If technical issues arise → Focus on celebrating effort and communication growth over perfection
lessons.troubleshooting: If performance anxiety is high, make it optional or offer alternative ways to showcase learning
lessons.realWorldConnection: Performers share their talents with audiences - celebrating what we've learned makes us proud
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by combining all communication skills

lessons.title: Portfolio de communication
lessons.oneGoal: Students reflect on their growth as French communicators

opening.activity: Review class performance success. Today look back at amazing communication journey from Lesson 1 to now!

mainActivity.activity: Portfolio creation - students compile examples of their communication growth, reflections on learning, and goals for continued French communication.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may create elaborate portfolios, others simple collections. Support all reflection styles.

closing.activity: Portfolio sharing - students share one thing they're most proud of in their communication growth.

decisionPoints: If students don't see their growth → Use specific examples and before/after comparisons
If portfolio creation overwhelming → Help them choose just 2-3 meaningful examples of growth
If students want to include everything → Guide them toward most significant learning moments
lessons.troubleshooting: If reflection feels abstract, use concrete examples like 'remember when you were shy to speak, now you love presenting!'
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can see how much better we've become at sharing ideas - like looking at old photos to see how we've grown
lessons.progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by reflecting on communication journey

lessons.title: Conteurs d'histoires
lessons.oneGoal: Students create and tell elaborate stories with multiple characters

opening.activity: Celebrate communication portfolio completion. Today become master storytellers creating elaborate tales!

mainActivity.activity: Advanced storytelling - students create and tell complex stories using multiple characters, different voices, and rich details. Focus on creative expression.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may create epic tales, others simple but creative stories. Celebrate all storytelling attempts.

closing.activity: Storyteller appreciation circle - audience gives specific compliments about storytelling techniques.

decisionPoints: If stories become too complex → Help students focus on 2-3 main characters and simple plot
If students struggle with creativity → Provide story starter prompts and character suggestions
If students want to tell very long stories → Help them practice concise, engaging storytelling
lessons.troubleshooting: If elaborate storytelling feels overwhelming, let students adapt familiar stories with their own creative twists
lessons.realWorldConnection: Storytellers entertain people with creative tales - sharing stories brings joy to listeners
lessons.progression: Extension - applies storytelling skills to complex narratives

lessons.title: Reporters de nouvelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students report on classroom or school events like news reporters

opening.activity: Review creative storytelling. Today be news reporters sharing real information about our school!

mainActivity.activity: News reporting - students research and report on classroom or school events using reporter techniques. Practice clear, informative communication.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may love reporter role, others prefer different communication styles. Support all approaches.

closing.activity: Evening news show - students present their news reports to 'television audience' (class).

decisionPoints: If students struggle finding news → Help them identify simple classroom or school events to report
If reports become too silly → Guide them toward respectful, informative reporting
If students nervous about formal reporting → Let them practice with partners first
lessons.troubleshooting: If news reporting feels too formal, start with sharing simple announcements or describing class activities
lessons.realWorldConnection: Reporters tell people about important events - sharing information helps our community stay connected
lessons.progression: Extension - uses communication skills for informational purposes

lessons.title: Débat amical
lessons.oneGoal: Students share different opinions respectfully on simple topics

opening.activity: Review news reporting. Today learn that people can have different ideas and still be friends!

mainActivity.activity: Gentle debate practice - students share different opinions on simple topics (favorite seasons, best playground games) while practicing respectful disagreement.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may enjoy debate, others prefer agreement. Support all comfort levels with different opinions.

closing.activity: Reflection on respectful disagreement - students share what they learned about different opinions.

decisionPoints: If students get upset about disagreement → Reinforce that different opinions are normal and okay
If students avoid sharing opinions → Provide very safe, low-stakes topics and encourage gentle participation
If debates become arguments → Model respectful language and redirect to listening skills
lessons.troubleshooting: If debate concept is too challenging, focus on sharing preferences and asking 'why do you think that?'
lessons.realWorldConnection: People can have different ideas and still be friends - listening to different opinions helps us learn
lessons.progression: Extension - explores respectful disagreement and discussion

lessons.title: Enseignants experts
lessons.oneGoal: Students teach younger students or family members something new

opening.activity: Review respectful opinion sharing. Today become teachers sharing expertise with others!

mainActivity.activity: Teaching practice - students plan and practice teaching something they know well to younger students, family members, or classmates.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students natural teachers, others need support organizing knowledge for teaching. Help all develop teaching skills.

closing.activity: Teacher appreciation - students reflect on what makes good teaching and how it feels to help others learn.

decisionPoints: If students can't think what to teach → Help them identify skills they've mastered (tying shoes, games, etc.)
If teaching feels overwhelming → Start with very simple skills or let them teach stuffed animals
If students frustrated when others don't learn quickly → Model patience and different teaching approaches
lessons.troubleshooting: If teaching concept is too abstract, let students demonstrate rather than formally teach
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can teach others what we've learned - sharing knowledge helps everyone grow
lessons.progression: Extension - uses communication skills to teach others

lessons.title: Ambassadeurs culturels
lessons.oneGoal: Students share aspects of their culture through creative communication

opening.activity: Review being teachers and experts. Today be cultural ambassadors sharing special traditions from our families!

mainActivity.activity: Cultural sharing - students present aspects of their family culture, traditions, or heritage using communication skills developed throughout unit.
mainActivity.flexibility: Some students may have rich cultural traditions to share, others simpler family customs. All sharing is valuable.

closing.activity: Cultural appreciation - celebrate the diversity in classroom and what we learned about each other's backgrounds.

decisionPoints: If students don't identify with specific culture → Help them share any family traditions or special customs
If students share very personal information → Guide with sensitivity and respect
If students feel left out → Emphasize that all families have special ways of doing things
lessons.troubleshooting: If cultural sharing feels uncomfortable, focus on simple family traditions like holiday celebrations or favorite foods
lessons.realWorldConnection: We can share our family traditions with others - learning about different cultures makes our community richer
lessons.progression: Extension - connects communication to cultural identity

lessons.title: Célébration de communicateurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students celebrate their growth as confident French communicators

opening.activity: Look back at incredible communication journey from shy beginners to confident communicators!

mainActivity.activity: Communication celebration - students showcase their favorite communication skills, receive certificates, and reflect on amazing growth as French speakers.
mainActivity.flexibility: Let students choose how they want to demonstrate their communication growth - all achievements celebrated equally.

closing.activity: Final circle: each student completes 'Je suis un communicateur confiant parce que...' Group celebration photo with certificates.

decisionPoints: If students don't feel confident → Point out specific examples of communication growth throughout unit
If students want to keep practicing → Encourage continued French communication in daily activities
If celebration feels overwhelming → Keep it simple with just recognition and certificate presentation
lessons.troubleshooting: If students don't recognize their progress, use before/after examples from beginning of unit
lessons.realWorldConnection: Confident communicators can share ideas with anyone - our voices can now reach the French-speaking world!
lessons.progression: Extension - culminates unit with celebration of communication growth
